questions.q: Explain the heating effect of electric current and its uses.
answer: When an electric current flows through a wire, the wire becomes hot. This is called the heating effect of current.

answer.text: The greater the resistance of the wire, the more heat is produced for a given current. Appliances that need to produce heat use a special high-resistance wire, often made of nichrome.
The heating effect is used in electric heaters, irons, geysers and toasters. In an electric bulb, current heats a thin tungsten filament until it glows and gives light.
The same effect makes the electric fuse a safety device: a thin wire in the fuse melts and breaks the circuit if too much current flows, preventing wires from overheating and causing fire.

questions.q: What is the magnetic effect of current, and how does an electromagnet work?
answer: A wire carrying an electric current behaves like a magnet; this is called the magnetic effect of current, first shown by Oersted, who saw a compass needle deflect near a current-carrying wire.

answer.text: An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of insulated wire around a piece of iron, called the core. When current flows through the coil, the iron becomes a strong magnet, and when the current is switched off, it loses its magnetism.
Because it can be switched on and off and made very strong, the electromagnet is used in cranes to lift iron, and in electric bells, motors and loudspeakers.

answer: Thus electricity and magnetism are closely linked.

questions.q: What is an electric circuit, and what do its common symbols represent?

answer.text: An electric circuit is a complete path along which electric current can flow. It usually consists of a cell or battery, connecting wires, a switch and a device such as a bulb. Current flows only when the circuit is complete and the switch is on; if there is a break, the current stops.

To draw circuits easily, we use standard symbols instead of pictures. A cell is shown by a long and a short line, a battery by two or more cells joined together, a bulb by a small circle with a cross, and a switch by a small gap with a lever that can be open or closed.
A drawing made with such symbols is called a circuit diagram.

answer: Thus an electric circuit is a complete path for current, and standard symbols are used to represent its parts in a circuit diagram.

questions.q: How does an electric bell work?

answer.text: An electric bell works using the magnetic effect of an electric current, that is, using an electromagnet, a coil that becomes a magnet when current flows through it.

When the circuit is switched on, current flows through the coil and turns it into a magnet. This electromagnet attracts an iron strip, and the hammer fixed to the strip strikes the gong, producing a sound. As the strip moves, it breaks the circuit at a contact point, so the current stops and the electromagnet loses its magnetism.
The strip then springs back, the circuit is completed again, and the process repeats rapidly, making the hammer strike the gong again and again, so the bell rings continuously.

answer: Thus an electric bell rings because an electromagnet repeatedly attracts and releases the hammer, which strikes the gong.
